John — thanks, and hi Dylan/Hiro. Below are our formal answers you can paste into Acme's questionnaire. I include specifics and an explanation of edge cases (backups, caches, and deletion timelines). I attached our full retention policy and SOC 2 reference documents for procurement.

1) Data residency (hosted API)
- Region options: For hosted customers we offer regional routing to keep data in the requested geographic region. Current production regions: US (us-west-2/us-east-1) and EU (eu-west-1). Customers may request EU-only processing via account configuration; we will route API traffic and store operational artifacts in the selected region.
- Note: Some transient runtime caches (in-memory KV caches) may exist on GPUs serving requests; those caches are ephemeral and scoped to the serving cluster in the selected region. No customer content is replicated to other regions for normal operation.

2) Retention windows (hosted API default)
- Request/response payloads: 30 days. We retain full request and response payloads for 30 days to support debugging, quality investigations, and abuse detection.
- Request metadata & usage logs: 90 days. Metadata (timestamps, token counts, model used, client IPs when not anonymized by the customer, request latency) is kept for 90 days to support billing reconciliation and operational analytics.
- Audit logs (control plane actions, config changes): 365 days.
- Backups & snapshots: up to 90 days. Backups are rotated; deletion requests start the process of removing data from primary systems immediately but backups may contain copies for up to the backup retention window.
- Embeddings and optional persisted indexes: By default, the hosted API does not persist embeddings or user vectors unless the customer uses Redwood-managed index services (opt-in). If you opt in, persisted embeddings are retained per the configured index policy.

3) Deletion and removal process
- Customer-initiated deletion: Open a support ticket (support@redwood.com) or raise a request through the Console. Provide account identifier and the scope (e.g., all request payloads between X and Y).
- Timeline: Primary data removal from live systems: up to 30 days from ticket confirmation. Propagation to logs and caches: typically within 72 hours for active systems. Backups may still contain data for up to 90 days; customers can request an accelerated retention review for critical cases and we will prioritize manual remediation where feasible.
- Certificate of deletion: We provide a deletion confirmation note with the ticket closure details (ticket ID and timestamp). For high-compliance customers we can include this as part of the security review package.

4) Use of customer data for model training
- Redwood does NOT use customer request/response payloads from the hosted API to train or improve our hosted model fleet. We maintain a strict policy that customer content is not incorporated into model training pipelines unless explicit, documented opt-in is obtained from the customer (and handled under separate Data Processing Addendum).

5) Encryption and keys
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ across all endpoints.
- At rest: AES-256. Hosted API keys and data are encrypted using Redwood-managed KMS keys. For Private deployments we offer BYOK integration; for hosted customers we can discuss dedicated keying options for enterprise plans.

6) Operational notes & exceptions
- For debugging escalations, engineers may request temporary access to specific request payloads; such access is logged, time-limited, and requires approval as described in our internal access control policy.
- Aggregated telemetry: We retain anonymized, aggregated telemetry to monitor model performance; aggregated data does not contain PII or raw customer payloads.

John — good questions. Confirming the specifics so procurement has clear items to sign off on: 

- Shorter retention windows: Yes. The 30-day request/response retention is our hosted default, but we can configure shorter windows (down to 7 days) for enterprise accounts during onboarding. Shorter windows may limit our ability to perform some debugging or quality investigations, which we will document and operationalize per account.
- Backup retention configuration: The 90-day backup retention is our standard practice for hosted backups. For enterprise customers we offer contractual changes to backup retention windows as part of an enterprise security addendum; this is handled case-by-case and will be included in the SOW or DPA.
- Training usage: Confirmed in writing — Redwood will not use hosted API customer payloads for model training unless the customer explicitly opts in and signs the relevant DPA/addendum. I have included the exact sentence you can paste into your questionnaire: "Redwood Inference does not use customer request or response payloads received via the hosted API for model training or improvement unless explicit, documented customer opt-in is obtained via a signed Data Processing Addendum."
